subject: Marketplace currency rounding causing negative payout — reconciliation request
messages:
From: marketplace-billing@marketplace.example.com
To: jonas_weber@example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@example.com, naomi_feldman@example.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: currency adjustments caused negative payout on 2026-05 USD->EUR settlement

Hi Jonas —

We were reconciling May settlement lines for Acme Cloud Solutions and flagged a set of automated rounding adjustments applied during the USD->EUR conversion that resulted in a negative net payout on the invoice (line items were credited back, then further FX rounding produced an overall negative amount).

Summary:
- Platform settlement ID: MPL-2026-05-ACME-4512
- Gross charges (USD): $12,384.50
- Marketplace fee (USD): $2,476.90
- Post-conversion EUR payout recorded: -€3.12 (negative)
- Evidence: attached CSV with raw usage rows and exchange-rate stamps

Could you confirm whether Redwood saw an offsetting debit/credit on your side (intercompany routing / withholding) or if this should be treated as a marketplace-generated credit we need to issue back to the seller? We have temporarily held the payout pending your confirmation; collections team has been notified.

Attachments: gcp_apr-may_usage_delta.csv

Thanks,
Aisha Romero
Marketplace Billing Lead
Marketplace Operations
marketplace-billing@marketplace.example.com

From: jonas_weber@example.com
To: marketplace-billing@marketplace.example.com, acme-finance@example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@example.com, naomi_feldman@example.com, priyom_das@example.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: currency adjustments caused negative payout on 2026-05 USD->EUR settlement

Thanks Aisha —

We saw the collections hold reflected in our payout dashboard this morning and have pulled the same raw usage lines through our internal ledger. A couple quick notes before we dig in:

1) We run dual-path attribution for marketplace meters (direct meter + reseller overlay). If both paths produced small, offsetting micro-credits, the FX conversion could amplify a net-negative when aggregated and rounded to two decimals.
2) We do not automatically reverse marketplace-issued credits on our side until we validate the seller claim.

I'm looping in Marissa (recon) and Naomi (tax/VAT) to confirm whether any EU VAT pass-through or withholding entries would create an offset. Priyom, can you pull the intercompany tags for MPL-2026-05-ACME-4512 and share any reconciliation workbook you have?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: run matching on usage_id and seller_id across the raw CSV and our ledger (please attach any reconciliation workbook)
- Naomi: confirm whether VAT/tax stamps on the marketplace-side credit create a netbook adjustment for EU entities
- Priyom: export intercompany tag list and timestamped ledger rows

We'd like to clear the collections hold by EOD Friday if there are no unresolved adjustments. Jonas

From: marissa_cole@example.com
To: jonas_weber@example.com, marketplace-billing@marketplace.example.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@example.com, priyom_das@example.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: currency adjustments caused negative payout on 2026-05 USD->EUR settlement

Jonas / Aisha —

I ran a quick pass and attached a working workbook (currency_recon_workbook_aug28.xlsx) with three tabs: raw-match, aggregated-fx, and rounding-impact. Key findings:

- There were 18 micro-credits (avg €0.17) generated when the marketplace applied per-usage refunds for a subset of failed provisioning events.
- On our side, two of those credits were tagged to a reseller overlay (seller_id SLR-998) that we treat as a contra-revenue entry; the marketplace tagged them as direct seller refunds. That mismatch caused a small double-count when both paths were tallied before FX conversion.
- Exchange-rate stamps show the marketplace applied the spot rate at 03:12 UTC while our conversion used the daily published mid-rate at 23:59 UTC. The intraday difference introduced a €0.41 swing.
- Net effect aggregated and rounded to cents produced the -€3.12 recorded.

Recommendation:
- Marketplace issues a 3.12 EUR credit memo to the seller (DocuSign link) OR we accept a debit to our reseller overlay to net the difference (requires marketplace acceptance).
- Naomi, tax impact? If the marketplace issues the credit, do we need a VAT-correction note for the EU entity?

I've attached audit_notes_jonas_20260828.pdf with sample row reconciliations.

Marissa
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: marketplace-billing@marketplace.example.com
To: jonas_weber@example.com, marissa_cole@example.com
Cc: acme-finance@example.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: currency adjustments caused negative payout on 2026-05 USD->EUR settlement

> Jonas / Aisha —
>
> I ran a quick pass and attached a working workbook ... Key findings:
> - There were 18 micro-credits ...
> - Exchange-rate stamps show the marketplace applied the spot rate ...

Thanks for the deep dive, Marissa — this is very helpful.

We can either:
A) Issue a formal credit memo for €3.12 to the seller (we will generate a VAT-corrected invoice if the original had VAT) — we can push a DocuSign credit memo to the seller by EOD tomorrow once you confirm wording.
B) Apply an internal debit to the reseller overlay and notify Redwood to accept the charge back (we will need Redwood billing contact signature for acceptance).

For speed, option A is quickest and removes the collections hold immediately. We will send a DocuSign link to the seller and copy Redwood once completed.

DocuSign preview (placeholder): https://docusign.example.com/preview/CM-2026-05-ACME-4512

Please confirm which path you prefer.

Thanks,
Aisha Romero
Marketplace Billing Lead

Aisha —

Thanks. We want to keep seller relationships clean and avoid retrospective chargebacks. Please proceed with option A (credit memo via DocuSign) and include a VAT-correction line so our tax team can reconcile.

Marissa — please confirm the exact credit memo text to Aisha (one-line reason: FX-induced rounding correction on 18 micro-refunds; amount €3.12). Naomi, please prepare a short VAT-notice we can attach to the credit so the seller and our EU entity have the audit trail. Priyom: once the DocuSign is complete, update the intercompany tags so our ledger picks up the reversal and we can remove the collections hold.

Target: remove collections hold within 24 hours of DocuSign completion.

Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
